_comment: The classification of every file whose change can affect exhaustive TLC (contract C1, #5148).
Globs are repository-relative, fnmatch-style: '*' matches any run of
characters INCLUDING '/', so '**' is equivalent and 'spec/*.md' matches every
markdown file at any depth under spec/. Only literal characters and '*' are
allowed, so every reader of this file matches identically.
Three classes. 'neutral' and 'routing' are exclusions, checked first:
- neutral: never affects a TLC run (refinement notes and READMEs TLC never reads,
Formal harness files no verdict-affecting or routing file references, workflow
files that select, route, provision and run nothing TLC checks).
- routing: decides which job runs which existing TLC case, or provisions and
launches legs, and cannot change a verdict or the set of cases. Must not pin
the TLA+ toolchain.
- verdictInputs: can change a TLC verdict or the set of cases that exist.
When unsure, a file is a verdict input.
A path is in 'verdictInputs' (or 'toolchain') when it matches one of that list's
globs and no 'neutral' or 'routing' glob. Every 'toolchain' glob is a
'verdictInputs' glob.
tier-scope.py runs exhaustive TLC when a pull request (or an integration-branch
push) changes a verdict input; a change touching only routing, neutral or
unclassified paths runs the base-model smoke shard instead, and the
toolchain-free TLC partition check (CiMemberPullRequestTieringTests) proves routing still
selects every TLC case exactly once. TlcInputClassificationTests requires every
file under test/lattice/Formal/, .github/workflows/ and .github/actions/ to be
classified exactly once. A new TLC-neutral Formal file uses a 'Refinement*' name
and is listed in 'neutral' explicitly.
